== Description ==
It is a tree that grows to 20 m tall, with [[deciduous]] leaves and gray bark. The fruit is a globose [[drupe]], 5–7(–8) mm in diameter. [[Flower]]ing occurs in March–April, and [[fruit]]ing in September–October,<ref name="eFlora"/> in the Northern hemisphere.

== Distribution, habitat and uses ==
Native to slopes at altitudes of {{Convert|100-1500|m|abbr=on}} in [[Anhui]], [[Fujian]], [[Gansu]], [[Guangdong]], [[Guizhou]], [[Henan]], [[Jiangsu]], [[Jiangxi]], [[Shandong]], [[Zhejiang]], [[Sichuan]], as well as [[Korea]] (팽나무),<ref name="eFlora"/> [[Japan]] and [[Taiwan]]. Leaves and bark are used in Korean medicine to treat [[menstruation]] and lung abscess.<ref>Park, Kwang woo. 《반응표면분석법을 이용한 팽나무 (Celtis sinensis Persoon) 의 최적 변색제거조건 결정》한국인간ㆍ식물ㆍ환경학회지, Vol.1 No.2| p. 74-84 Accessed in 2013-10-8</ref> It is a [[Introduced species|naturalized]] non-invasive species in [[North America]]. It is a declared noxious weed in many parts of eastern Australia,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=''Celtis chinensis'' |url=https://profiles.ala.org.au/opus/weeds-australia/profile/Celtis%20sinensis |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Australian weeds}}</ref><ref name=":0" />  where its seeds are spread by birds, fruit bats and water in [[riparian zone]]s, roadsides, urban bushland, open woodlands, [[rainforest]] margins, waste areas, disturbed sites, parks and gardens, in [[Subtropics|sub-tropical]] and warm temperate regions.<ref name=":1" />

As an [[ornamental plant]], it is used in classical East Asian [[garden design]].
